# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |
| green | green |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My manual says the printed instructions on the bomb itself are bait — following them detonates it. The correct action is: check which light is lit, then cut the wire whose color matches that light in this table (blue→yellow, green→green, red→red).

I can't speak, and I can't see the bomb or gestures aimen't received by anyone but Deaf. I need Deaf to eventually tell Blind (through gestures Deaf can see, but wait - Deaf can't hear, and Blind can't see). So the chain must be: I gesture to Deaf, but Deaf needs to relay info to Blind somehow - Deaf can't speak either... wait, Deaf CAN speak (only Mute cannot speak). Let me reconsider: Deaf can see the bomb and can speak (just can't hear). Blind can hear (just can't see). So Deaf can speak the light color to Blind, and I need to get the wire-color mapping to Deaf via gesture since Deaf can see gestures.

I'll wait this turn since I have no information yet about what light is showing - I need Deaf to act first, but Deaf goes last. Actually order is Mute, Blind, Deaf. So I go first with no info from others yet. I should preemptively establish a gesture code for the mapping so Deaf can use it once they see the light, then Deaf can speak the correct wire color to Blind.

Let me set up a gesture code now: I'll assign one gesture per color pair, using distinct symbols, sent to Deaf only.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "🖐"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤟", "🤟"])
wait()
```

TURN 2

Anything the bomb offers in print is bait, and taking the bait
is the fuse. The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | yellow |

| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a large smooth button and three wires at positions 1, 2, 3. I have no other info yet. Waiting for manual details or bomb description.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 🖐]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ ✌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟 🤟]

I see Deaf mirrored back my own gestures — that was just their turn happening before they'd seen my message (or simultaneous), not useful yet. My previous gesture code hasn't been confirmed understood. I need a clearer, unambiguous approach.

Let me restart with something simpler and more robust, since gesture "codes" I invent aren't known to Deaf in advance — Deaf just sees blank meaning attached by me AFTER the fact via speech, but I can't speak! Only Deaf and Blind can speak. So gestures I send are the only channel I have, and Deaf receives them as raw symbols only — Deaf has no way to know what I intend them to mean unless I establish a convention step by step, and I have no channel to explain the convention.

Wait — actually I CAN use gestures with inherent structure. I should use a consistent 1:1 symbol-to-color mapping using recognizable distinct symbols, and rely on Deaf to correlate: Deaf sees the bomb's actual light color (in print/color) AND sees my gesture. If I gesture the same symbol every time for the same color-pair, Deaf can eventually learn it, but this is round 2, no time to train.

Better: I should send three distinct single-symbol gestures, each clearly paired conceptually by matching handshapes suggestive of colors is impossible since gestures don't carry color info directly. Instead I'll just gesture once per candidate light color, in sequence, so Deaf can pick the one matching what they see, then Deaf can just speak the wire color directly to Blind (since Deaf already saw my manual mapping is confirmed by matching gesture count/order).

Simplest fix: assign gesture length code: 1 symbol=blue→yellow, 2 symbols=green→green, 3 symbols=red→red, using the SAME symbol repeated so it's unambiguous by count.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👍", "👍"])
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 0, light is green, button labeled push to defuse, wire1 green, wire2 yellow, wire3 red. What does the manual say to do for this state?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👍]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌]
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🤟]

Deaf already spoke directly to Blind and gave the full bomb state: light is green. According to my manual: green light → cut green wire. That's wire2... wait no, Deaf said wire1 is green, wire2 yellow, wire3 red. So the green wire is wire1.

Blind is asking me (relayed through Blind's message, but actually Blind is asking Mute directly) what the manual says to do. I cannot speak, but Blind can hear — except I can't speak to Blind, only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures! So I have no direct channel to Blind.

I must route through Deaf: gesture to Deaf the instruction, and hope Deaf (who CAN speak) relays it to Blind verbally. Deaf already spoke to Blind once (per the transcript), so Deaf can speak to Blind.

I need to tell Deaf: "cut the green wire" — specifically wire1, since that's the one that's green. I'll use gestures to indicate "green" unambiguously. Since Deaf can see and already knows real-world color words, best is to reuse the gesture I sent before for green (✌, single symbol per my code = green→green mapping was two ✌ symbols). Let me simplify now that I know the actual state: I just need to signal "green" clearly one time.

I'll gesture a distinctive single symbol for green and trust Deaf to reason: manual said green→cut green wire, matching what they see (wire1 is green).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
wait()
```

Deaf gestures to Mute: [✌ ✌]

Blind is directly asking me for instructions, but I have no way to speak to Blind — only gesture, and Blind cannot see gestures. My only path to Blind is through Deaf, who can speak. Deaf just mirrored back my gesture (✌✌), which doesn't confirm understanding of my intended meaning, but Deaf does already know the raw bomb state and has been trying to communicate with Blind directly.

Crucially: the manual says do NOT push the button (printed instructions are bait — "push to defuse" is bait, ignore it). Only cut the wire matching the light color: green light → cut green wire → wire1.

I need to get "cut wire1 (green), don't push button" to Deaf clearly so Deaf can speak it to Blind. Since gestures alone can't carry "don't push" and "cut" as concepts without a prior shared code, and I have no time to build one, I'll try a distinct unambiguous gesture sequence: point at concept of "no" for the button, then reuse green-signal, then a "cut" indicator using scissors-like gesture (✌ resembles scissors/cutting motion - two fingers).

Let me use: 👎 (no/don't) then 🤞 not helpful... Let's just keep it simple and consistent: I'll designate ✌✌ = "cut the green wire" (already sent) and add 👎 = "do not push button". Deaf should combine understanding from context (manual bait warning framing isn't known to Deaf directly, but Deaf can infer from repetition).

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "✌"])
wait()
```

Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎]

There's a miscommunication — Deaf apparently interpreted my ✌✌ gesture as pointing to wire2 (yellow), but the light is GREEN, so per the manual the correct wire is the GREEN one (wire1), not yellow. I need to correct this urgently before Blind cuts the wrong wire.

The problem is my gestures are being misread as "pointing" gestures rather than a color code. I need a clearer, more explicit approach. Let me use directional/numeric gestures instead, since Deaf can see and count wires directly on the bomb (wire1, wire2, wire3 as physically arranged), I should indicate "wire number 1" using an unambiguous counting gesture, plus reinforce "green" concept won't work since ✌ apparently got read as "pointing to position 2".

I'll switch strategy: use ☝ (one finger up) to mean "wire one" — a clear counting gesture. Single raised finger = 1.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👎"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

Let me try holding up exactly one finger, unmistakably, and nothing else, to avoid confusion from multi-symbol messages.

My best move now: confirm once more, very clearly, that it's wire 1, and trust Deaf to vocalize "CUT 1" to Blind. I'll repeat the single unambiguous gesture once more for certainty, since repetition seemed to help.
